newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 1996 operational deficit at 3.89 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1996 operational deficit at 3.89 pct of GDP.

text.p: Brazil posted a public sector operational deficit of 29.229 billion reais in 1996, equivalent to 3.89 percent of Gross Domestic Product, the Central Bank said.
That result compared with widespread expectations of an operational deficit of at least 4.5 percent of GDP.
The bank said in a statement that net public sector debt ended 1996 at 268.97 billion reais, or 34.5 percent of GDP.
It added that the monetary base expanded 2.6 percent in January, according to daily averages.

The bank statement said that the federal government posted an operational deficit of 1.67 percent of GDP, the states and municipalities a deficit of 1.89 percent and state firms a shortfall 0.33 percent of GDP.
The consolidated public sector primary results, which does not include interest payments, was a 0.09 percent of GDP deficit, the Central Bank said.
In primary terms the federal government posted a 0.41 percent of GDP surplus, state governments and cities a 0.57 percent deficit and state firms a small surplus of 0.07 percent.
The bank said that the public sector posted a deficit in 1995 of 4.79 percent of GDP.
The public sector borrowing requirements (PSBR) in 1996 was 45.749 billion reais, equivalent the Central Bank said to 6.09 percent of GDP.

The bank said that net internal debt at the end of 1996 stood at 237.457 billion reais or 30.4 percent of GDP, slightly up from 30.2 percent of GDP in November and way above 1995 levels of 170.31 billion reais or 24.5 percent of GDP internal debt stock.

Net external debt ended 1996 at 31.514 billion reais or 4 percent of GDP. That was virtually unchanged in terms of GDP from November and lower than 1995 levels of 38.132 billion reais or 5.5 percent of GDP.
The statement said that the monetary base expansion in January was charecterized by a surge on the last day of the month, a Friday.
It said that a month to month contraction of 3.8 percent seen up to Jan 30 turned into a month on month 20.5 percent expansion on Jan 31.
The bank said the monetary base in January was of 20.62 billion reais.
